record.context_brief: Sparse-incidence clique coverings of almost all graphs.
record.original_question: For almost every graph on n vertices, does there exist a collection of cliques such that each vertex belongs to only o(n) of the chosen cliques while all but o(n^2) edges are covered by those cliques? More sharply, can one achieve a per-vertex bound of order O(n / log n)?

evidence.quote: Can one find cliques with each vertex in o(n) cliques such that o(n^2) edges are uncovered? The best possible result would be f(n) = O(n/log n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G(n,1/2)$ denote the random graph on the vertex set $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ in which each pair of distinct vertices is joined by an edge independently with probability $1/2$. A clique of $G$ is a subset of vertices that is pairwise adjacent. A clique covering of $G$ is a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of cliques of $G$ whose union of edge sets covers some subset of the edges of $G$; an edge of $G$ is said to be covered by $\mathcal{C}$ if it is contained in at least one clique of $\mathcal{C}$. For a vertex $v$, let $d_{\mathcal{C}}(v)$ denote the number of cliques in $\mathcal{C}$ that contain $v$.

Prove or disprove: with probability tending to $1$ as $n 	o \infty$, the random graph $G(n,1/2)$ admits a collection of cliques $\mathcal{C}$ such that

(i) $\max_{v} d_{\mathcal{C}}(v) = o(n)$, and

(ii) all but $o(n^2)$ edges of $G$ are covered by $\mathcal{C}$.

Moreover, determine whether one can sharpen (i) to $\max_{v} d_{\mathcal{C}}(v) = O(n/\log n)$, while still satisfying (ii).
artifact.status_search_result: Related results are known: Bollobás–Erdős–Spencer–West (1993) bounded the total number of cliques needed to cover almost all edges of $G(n,1/2)$, and Frieze–Reed (1995) determined that the clique cover number of $G(n,1/2)$ is $\Theta(n^2/\log^2 n)$. However, no source explicitly confirms a per-vertex incidence bound of the form $O(n/\log n)$ while leaving only $o(n^2)$ edges uncovered. The sharp form of the question therefore appears not to be definitively settled in accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Clique coverings of the edges of a random graph
status_evidence.snippet: Bollobás, Erdős, Spencer, West: edges of G(n,1/2) can be covered with O(n^2 log log n / (log n)^2) cliques.
status_evidence.claim: Total clique cover bound established, but per-vertex sharp bound not stated.

status_evidence.title: Covering the edges of a random graph by cliques (Frieze–Reed)
status_evidence.snippet: Clique cover number of G(n,p) is Theta(n^2/log^2 n) whp.
status_evidence.claim: Determines clique cover number; does not directly address per-vertex incidence bound O(n/log n).
